Hi Dave / Anne —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached is our first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the technical evaluation milestone. I pulled together the concrete milestones we discussed, proposed owners on both sides, and the preliminary success criteria so your team can quickly review and confirm.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: 3-week technical POC to validate latency, cost, and output quality for the DataGrid retrieval-assisted generation flows.
- Target close (commercial): 2026-10-01 (preliminary) — MAP aligns technical sign-off to commercial milestones.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft)
1) Kickoff & environment access (owner: DataGrid / Anne) — target: 2026-08-25
2) Baseline benchmark run (owner: Redwood / Karthik) — target: 2026-08-31
3) Model shortlist validation + configuration (owner: joint) — target: 2026-09-07
4) Cost & latency optimization pass (owner: Redwood) — target: 2026-09-14
5) Final evaluation readout / sign-off (owner: DataGrid + Redwood) — target: 2026-09-21

Key dependencies: customer VPN/VPC access, sample dataset (10k queries), SLA for token consumption during POC, and a single technical contact on your side for quick clarifications.

Attachments: DataGrid_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP with milestone table & acceptance criteria).

Next steps: please review and suggest edits inline in the PDF or reply with changes. If this looks OK, I’ll loop in Karthik to schedule the baseline benchmark run and share the benchmark spec worksheet.

Thanks —
Aisha

On Thu, 20 Aug 2026 at 11:08, Aisha Rahman wrote:
> I’ve also added Karthik as the Redwood technical owner for the baseline benchmark and the cost/latency optimization milestone. Karthik — can you take the baseline spec and drop the benchmark-specs.xlsx back with concrete success criteria...

Thanks Aisha — attaching the benchmark-specs.xlsx and a short CSV with the initial model shortlist (redwood-model-shortlist.csv). High-level summary below.

Benchmark success criteria (baseline + pass/fail thresholds)
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms on supplied 4k prompt distribution (env: dedicated hosted cluster, burst concurrency up to 32) — PASS if p95 < 120ms
- Quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.62 on the 500 labeled test prompts OR human accept rate >= 85% on a 100-sample blind set — PASS if either quality metric met
- Cost: <= $0.45 per 1k output tokens at baseline config — PASS if cost <= target after initial quantization/slot tuning
- Throughput: sustain >= 75 tokens/sec per GPU for longer-running batch workloads

Initial model shortlist (notes):
- rw-v1-large-quant (likely best latency/cost tradeoff)
- rw-v1-medium-tuned (better quality, slightly higher latency)
- qllama-70b-8bit (for quality stress test only — expect higher latency)

Benchmark plan & timeline
- Baseline run (owner: Redwood / Karthik): week of 2026-08-29 — run 10k queries, capture p50/p95/throughput, and cost estimates
- Optimization pass (owner: Redwood): week of 2026-09-07 — apply caching, continuous batching and one quantization profile to hit cost/latency target
- Readout (joint): 2026-09-14 — 30m readout + next-step decision.

Attachments included: benchmark-specs.xlsx (detailed test matrix), redwood-model-shortlist.csv. I’ll upload a copy to the HubSpot deal and link it in the MAP as well.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
